title: Bid anticipation, information revelation, and merger gains
primary_theories: neoclassical theory of mergers and acquisitions

rival_explanations: agency cost theory and hubris theory

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (U.S. publicly traded acquirers and targets)
context.sample_description: U.S. M&A bids from Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum merged with the CRSP/Compustat merged data set; both acquirer and target U.S. publicly traded firms; deals classified as mergers (not tender offers or block trades); acquirer seeks more than 50% of target shares to gain control and holds less than 50% beforehand; deal value exceeds one million dollars

data_sources.name: Manually collected bid-termination reasons (endogenous vs. exogenous failure classification, from Factiva, LexisNexis, Google news, and SDC Platinum deal synopsis/history)

analyses.label: Table 2: Parameter estimates (Simulated Method of Moments, SMM)
analyses.shock_or_instrument: exogenously failed bids (deals failing for reasons outside the control of the two firms) provide the cleanest identification, since exogenous bid failure reveals no new information and the drop in market value reflects only the lost merger gains
analyses.sample: 7185 bids (6050 successful, 1135 failed), 1980-2012; failed-bid subsamples used for identification: 143 exogenously failed, 334 endogenously failed

dv.name: empirical moments matched in SMM
dv.source: Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum; CRSP/Compustat merged data set

key_ivs.name: Search cost (C)
key_ivs.measure: search cost parameter estimated via SMM

key_ivs.name: Acquirer's share of merger gains / bargaining power (theta)
Arrival rate of random matching (lambda)
key_ivs.measure: arrival rate of random matching between potential acquirers and targets

key_ivs.name: Volatility of shocks to seeds (sigma_s)
key_ivs.measure: standard deviation of shocks to seeds

key_ivs.name: Volatility of shocks to productivity (sigma_z)
key_ivs.measure: standard deviation of shocks to productivity

controls.name: Concavity of production function alpha fixed to 0.7
Probability of exogenous bid termination iota (set to number of exogenously terminated bids divided by total number of bids)
Long-run average productivity z-bar normalized to zero

dv.name: empirical moments vs model-implied moments
dv.measure: 14 moments compared row-by-row (empirical estimate, simulated value, std. err., t-stat testing empirical = simulated); Panel B reports the chi-square/J-test of over-identifying restrictions (eight parameters estimated using 14 moments; J-test p-value = 9.32%)
dv.source: Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum; CRSP/Compustat merged data set

analyses.label: Table 4 (Panels A-C): Model-implied decomposition of announcement returns into merger gain and revelation effect; variance decompositions

dv.name: announcement returns of acquirers and targets
dv.measure: model-implied three-day announcement returns decomposed into merger gain and revelation effect (Panel A); variance of announcement returns decomposed into Var(merger gain), Var(revelation), 2Cov (Panel B); revelation-effect variance decomposed into s_Rev, z_Rev, and cross term (Panel C)
dv.source: estimated structural model (matched to CRSP three-day CAR)

key_ivs.name: Merger gain
key_ivs.measure: model-implied unexpected merger gain component of announcement return

key_ivs.name: Revelation effect
key_ivs.measure: model-implied revelation effect (news about the firm's stand-alone value revealed at announcement)

key_ivs.name: Shocks to seeds (s) vs. shocks to productivity (z)
key_ivs.measure: revelation-effect variance attributed to shocks to s (s_Rev), shocks to z (z_Rev), and their cross-effect

analyses.label: Table 4 Panel D: Spillover effect - model (-0.19%) vs. data test using matched standalone firms' three-day CAR
analyses.sample: matched standalone firms (same-industry peers not in any M&A during [-1,1] years) around bid announcements

key_ivs.name: Being a matched standalone peer around a bid announcement

analyses.label: Table 5 Panel A: Acquirer size effect (announcement returns of large vs. small acquirers, model vs. data)
analyses.sample: acquirers split into top vs. bottom size terciles

dv.name: acquirer announcement return
dv.measure: average announcement return by acquirer size group, decomposed into merger gain and revelation effect (model), compared to data
dv.source: estimated structural model; data three-day CAR (CRSP)

key_ivs.name: Acquirer size group
key_ivs.measure: large acquirer group = acquirers with size in the top tercile; small acquirer group = bottom tercile

analyses.label: Table 5 Panel B: Predictability of M&As (predictive regression of acquirer/target dummy on ROA and size)
analyses.sample: model-simulated panel data of firms and actual data (R-squared reported for acquirer and target regressions)

dv.name: acquirer or target dummy
dv.source: Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum; CRSP/Compustat (model-simulated panel and actual data)

key_ivs.name: Size at t-1
key_ivs.measure: the firm's size at period t-1

analyses.label: Section 5.1 / Robustness: re-estimation including hubris motive and agency costs
analyses.sample: baseline estimation sample augmented with hubris moments (first moment 143 obs; moments 2-4 22 obs)

dv.name: empirical moments including hubristic-acquisition moments
dv.source: Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum; CRSP/Compustat merged data set

key_ivs.name: Hubris parameter (eta) and hubris threshold (m)
key_ivs.measure: eta estimated jointly via SMM; m calibrated to 1.68 standard deviations above the mean of z and s
